A single-line defect that silently breaks the entire production data path, and the only claim in this packet that survives contact with `docker compose config`. docker-compose.prod.yml:5 sets the pooler's upstream as `DATABASE_URL=postgres://${POSTGRES_USER}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}`, and every backend-side service points at the pooler (docker-compose.prod.yml:36, 93, 150, 185, 220, 255, 290). Rendered config confirms the dangling reference: `DATABASE_URL: postgres://<redacted>@db:5432/neondb`. `docker compose config` validates structure only and does not resolve service DNS, so this parses cleanly and would fail at runtime — the prod stack cannot bring up its connection pooler. Contrast: in docker-compose.yml the `db` service IS defined (L3-17), and docker-compose.override.yml's pgbouncer depends on that same `db` and resolves correctly, so the prior pass's 'undefined service db' report was accurate about the prod file only.
